schema_ddl:
CREATE TABLE INSURANCE (
    PID INT,
    TIV_2015 NUMERIC,
    TIV_2016 NUMERIC,
    LAT NUMERIC,
    LON NUMERIC,
    PRIMARY KEY (PID),
    CHECK (TIV_2015 >= 0),
    CHECK (TIV_2016 >= 0)
);
q1: SELECT ROUND(SUM(TIV_2016),2) TIV_2016 FROM INSURANCE WHERE TIV_2015 IN (SELECT TIV_2015 FROM INSURANCE GROUP BY TIV_2015 HAVING COUNT(*)>1) AND (LAT,LON) IN (SELECT LAT,LON FROM INSURANCE GROUP BY LAT,LON HAVING COUNT(*)=1)
q2: SELECT SUM(TIV_2016) AS TIV_2016 FROM INSURANCE AS A WHERE 1 <= ( SELECT COUNT(*) FROM INSURANCE WHERE A.PID != PID AND TIV_2015 = A.TIV_2015 ) AND (A.LAT, A.LON) NOT IN ( SELECT LAT, LON FROM INSURANCE WHERE A.PID != PID )
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT ROUND(SUM(TIV_2016),2) TIV_2016 FROM INSURANCE WHERE TIV_2015 IN (SELECT TIV_2015 FROM INSURANCE GROUP BY TIV_2015 HAVING COUNT(*)>1) AND (LAT,LON) IN (SELECT LAT,LON FROM INSURANCE GROUP BY LAT,LON HAVING COUNT(*)=1)
q2_prompt_sql: SELECT SUM(TIV_2016) AS TIV_2016 FROM INSURANCE AS A WHERE 1 <= ( SELECT COUNT(*) FROM INSURANCE WHERE A.PID != PID AND TIV_2015 = A.TIV_2015 ) AND (A.LAT, A.LON) NOT IN ( SELECT LAT, LON FROM INSURANCE WHERE A.PID != PID )
counterexample: INSERT INTO INSURANCE (PID, TIV_2015, TIV_2016, LAT, LON) VALUES (1, 1000, 1500.75, 40.7128, -74.0060); INSERT INTO INSURANCE (PID, TIV_2015, TIV_2016, LAT, LON) VALUES (2, 1000, 1500.76, 34.0522, -118.2437);
explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not semantically equivalent because Q1 rounds the sum of TIV_2016 to 2 decimal places, while Q2 does not round the sum. Additionally, Q1 uses IN with subqueries for TIV_2015 and (LAT, LON), while Q2 uses EXISTS with subqueries for TIV_2015 and (LAT, LON).
counterexample_dsp: The test data should have at least two policies with the same TIV_2015 value and different (LAT, LON) values. The sum of TIV_2016 for these policies should be a number that rounds differently when rounded to 2 decimal places in Q1 compared to Q2.
